newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden hopes to create 50,000 new 'green' jobs.
newsitem.headline: Sweden hopes to create 50,000 new 'green' jobs.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson is hoping to create up to 50,000 new jobs in the coming three years through a programme to improve Sweden's environmental performance, a Swedish newspaper said on Friday.
Persson was expected on Friday for the first time to lay down plans in more concrete terms on how he wanted to develop his ideas to make Sweden a pioneer in ecology, Dagens Industri said.
Persson was to speak at an environment seminar in Stockholm on Friday.
A six billion crown sum that Environment Minister Anna Lindh's ecology group has been granted to invest in the environment was expected to aim to create 48,000 new jobs over three years.
Persson has pledged to halve unemployment to around four percent by the year 2000.
In February Sweden's unemployment rate was 8.8 percent.
March's unemployment figures were due out at 1100 GMT on April 11.
